memory_update.text: POWL should be promoted as the cleanest underfollowed/direct electrical-equipment candidate for the data-center switchgear and power-distribution node because the evidence includes specific data-center orders, backlog, and book-to-bill signals.
VRT should remain a reference anchor, not the main alpha-discovery target, because it is the obvious high-attention mega-cap public-market leader in data-center critical power and infrastructure.
IESC is a second-order execution-services candidate: include in later layers only if filings continue to show data-center-driven revenue, favorable margins, and remaining performance obligations.

ATKR requires stronger evidence before promotion: current support shows data-center end-market participation but not enough quantification of data-center revenue mix, backlog, or hyperscale order pull-through.

The node’s strongest falsification variables are backlog quality, repeatability of mega-orders, gross-margin preservation, capacity-expansion timing, long-lead components, skilled-labor availability, and customer concentration.

node: Data-center electrical equipment: switchgear, transformers, busway, backup power, and power distribution
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the data-center electrical-equipment node. The strongest evidence in this pass is not from AI narratives but from hard order/backlog signals: Powell Industries disclosed multiple data-center infrastructure orders, including a post-quarter order above $400 million, while Vertiv provides the obvious reference exposure through power management, switchgear, busbar, UPS, rack power distribution, and integrated data-center infrastructure. The underfollowed lane is narrower than the broad AI-infrastructure story suggests: Powell, IES Holdings, and Atkore each have plausible direct or second-order exposure, but they require different validation paths. Powell is the cleanest order/backlog signal; IES is an execution-services and electrical-systems beneficiary; Atkore is a lower-conviction component/channel exposure that needs data-center mix verification.
